name: Kotak Mahindra Bank Ltd.
business_summary: Diversified financial group led by Kotak Mahindra Bank (retail, commercial, corporate banking, treasury) with subsidiaries in vehicle finance (Kotak Prime/Investments), broking, investment banking, asset management, life and general insurance. Q2 FY27 advances +24.7% and deposits +23.2% YoY; consolidated PAT Rs 5,645 cr (+26%). Anup Kumar Saha named MD & CEO with RBI approval (30 Sep 2026), ending leadership uncertainty. Sector-wide FCNR(B) inflows are inflating deposits but pressuring NIM into Q3.

revenue_mix.segment: Subsidiaries (Prime, Securities, AMC, IB, Life, General)

cost_structure.note: interest expense ~45% of revenue (Rs 31,143 cr TTM interest of Rs 73,545 cr revenue)

exposures.mechanism: +3pp system loan growth: Kotak is growing ~24.7% YoY (Q2 update) so its loan growth is partly share gain, system-beta ~1.2; +3pp -> NII +3.5% -> PPOP +4.5%; ROE-multiple flows via P/B; persistence 0.7 (growth compounds) -> ~+3.1.

+25bp repo: ~35-40% of book is EBLR/repo-linked and reprices in ~1 quarter (model knowledge) while term deposits reprice over 12m; gross NIM +3-5bp near term (+1.5% NII) but FCNR(B) cost drag (management: further Q3 pressure) and later deposit repricing offset; higher-for-longer also lifts discount rate. Net ~+1.0, wide.

evidence.note: RBI hiked repo 25bp to 5.50%, stance 'calibrated tightening' (Reuters/The Hindu headlines)
Kotak: FCNR(B) deposits to pressure Q3 margins; repo repricing and deployment to help (ET BFSI)

exposures.mechanism: Empirical -0.98/SSU (t -0.8) is insignificant; Fed path matters via FPI flows (FII 24.65%, falling) and FCNR(B) refinancing cost. Small negative.

Credit cost +50bp on loans ~Rs 5 lakh cr (model knowledge) = ~Rs 2,500 cr vs standalone PBT ~Rs 22,000 cr (TTM PAT Rs 21.5k cr cons.) -> PBT -11%; persistence 0.6; no EV gearing for banks -> ~-7. Q2 asset quality improved (The Hindu), so starting point is benign.

evidence.note: Q2 FY27 consolidated PAT Rs 5,645 cr (+26%); standalone Rs 4,212 cr (+29%); asset quality better

exposures.mechanism: Unsecured retail/cards/PL run down after FY24-25 tightening, still ~8-10% of advances (model knowledge, unverified). +1pp delinquencies on that slice at 60% LGD = ~0.05% of loans ~ -2% PBT; persistence 0.6 -> ~-1.2, rounded to -1.5 for contagion to sentiment.
+3pp system deposit growth eases liquidity and CD/FCNR dependence; Kotak deposits +23.2% (Q2 update) already outpacing system; modest +1.2.
+25bp 10y: AFS/FVTPL book ~Rs 40-50k cr at duration ~2 (model knowledge) -> MTM ~-Rs 250 cr (~-1% PBT); partly offset by reinvestment yield; also raises P/B discount rate. Net ~-0.7.
Kotak Securities/AMC/Investment Banking/Life ~10% of group PAT (model knowledge); +20% market activity -> +10% fee income there -> +1% group PAT; persistence 0.8 -> ~+0.8.

Kotak was barred from onboarding via digital channels / issuing new cards in Apr 2024 (model knowledge) and later cleared; a fresh tightening step (IT/KYC, unsecured risk-weights) carries asymmetric downside; 1 step ~-2 expected, tail -6.
FIIs hold 24.65% (falling from 26.4% in Mar-26); +US$5bn/qtr FPI inflows historically lift large private banks ~1.5-2.5% beyond beta; FPI selling was a drag in 2026.
+1pp GDP growth -> +1.5pp loan growth and better asset quality -> ~+2 to +4% equity; RBI raised FY27 growth forecast to 7.1% (Oct policy).

evidence.note: RBI hiked repo 25bp to 5.50%, stance 'calibrated tightening' (Reuters/The Hindu headlines)

exposures.mechanism: +5 VIX pts -> Nifty ~-3.5%; Kotak beta ~0.7-0.8 per the pack -> ~-2.6; partially offset by defensive quality bid; use -2.2.
Little direct FX; rupee weakness raises FCNR(B) liability valuation but swap-hedged (RBI swap window); sentiment effect via FPI. Small negative.

current_state.trend: Loan growth accelerating (24.7%), deposits +23.2%, profit +26% y/y, asset quality improving; margin to be pressured by FCNR in Q3 before repo repricing helps
current_state.valuation: P/E 21.9, P/B ~2.4 (price 466 vs BV 196 per screener; stock +18.5% in 3m, near 52w high 469); premium to PSU banks, in line with large private peers

Rate-hike cycle raising cost of deposits faster than asset repricing
upside_triggers: NIM trough in Q3 followed by EBLR repricing tailwind
Sustained 20%+ loan growth with improving credit cost
Clear strategy from new CEO; subsidiary value unlock
